accuracy.reason: All five objectives accurately distinguish interaction roles, protocol/application semantics, session locality, dependencies and uncertainty; no capacity or delivery guarantees are invented.

evidence.quote: Client and server describe roles. When a server calls another service, it acts as a client.

mechanisms.reason: Roles switch on downstream calls; HTTP fields carry operation/target/context; local-only sessions depend on one handler while externalized state introduces shared storage; overload and lost response are traced to consequences.

evidence.quote: Stateless does not mean no stored data. Stateless servers can use a shared database.

coherence.reason: Cards build from roles to protocol to session state, then costs and a full request explanation. Diagram source agrees with response direction, server-side access checks and state placement. Shared rendering assets are unchanged and inspected, not executed.

evidence.quote: Connect the request, responsibilities, data and outcome. Component names alone do not explain behavior.

decisions.reason: Cards 2-5 explain server trust checks, replaceable-handler benefits and storage dependency, local/offline work costs and safe uncertainty about retries. These support choosing responsibility and state placement.

evidence.quote: Choose where each task runs based on its needs. Keep trusted checks on the server. Use the client for work that needs a fast response or must work offline.

clarity.reason: All key terms are defined at first use, the role distinction is concise and the five cards avoid needless detail while supporting a complete application interaction.

evidence.quote: The server must check what each user can access. A hidden button does not prevent someone from sending a request.

outcomes.reason: Learner covers both roles, same/different machines and downstream role switching, protocol rules, every HTTP request/response field and application-specific success/error meanings.

Learner defines sessions, traces local-only session loss/rerouting, supplies request/shared context for stateless handlers, retains database/auth/storage dependency, and explains centralized reuse plus latency/unavailability/overload without automatic scalability.

Learner constructs a shared-data update with method/target/input, server access checks and allowed work, distinguishes persistent data/session context, returns interpreted outcome and keeps no-response uncertainty distinct from an explicit error.

sourceChecks.claim: Live RFC 9110 section 3.3 defines client request initiation and server response handling as program roles; intermediary requirements show a server also makes client requests. Same-host deployment does not change those roles.

Live RFC 9110 sections 1.3 and 3 describe semantics and request/response components; method/target/status/header/content roles are supported. MDN server-side introduction supports resource access checks separate from client UI.

Live Azure autoscaling explicitly warns not to depend on a particular instance or request affinity and recommends stateless services; session-memory and shared-store consequences follow from the stated process-memory prerequisite.

Live MDN server-side introduction explains common shared data, centralized server logic and access control; Azure scaling guidance explains bottlenecks and finite resources. Network delay/unavailability costs follow from explicit prerequisites.

Live RFC 9110 section 9.2.2 explicitly discusses retry after failure before receiving a response even when the first request succeeded. The deck correctly separates reported error from missing-response uncertainty.
